key_insight: EgoForge builds a goal‑conditioned egocentric world model that jointly predicts hands, objects, and viewpoint motion so it can simulate coherent, intent‑driven first‑person video rollouts over procedure‑scale horizons.
problem_solved: Models of egocentric video struggle with rapid camera motion, frequent hand–object interactions, and latent human intent; EgoForge addresses these to produce long‑horizon, goal‑directed egocentric simulations.
method: Learn a compact scene representation that separates agent (head/camera + hands) dynamics from object and environment state to handle rapid viewpoint changes and contact events.
Infer latent goals/intent from partial observations and condition a generative dynamics model to produce goal‑directed future states and rendered egocentric frames.
Train using multi‑task/self‑supervised objectives that emphasize physical consistency of interactions and temporal coherence rather than dense trajectory supervision.
impact: Enables realistic, actionable first‑person video prediction useful for imitation learning, AR/VR content generation, and robotic planning from human demonstrations with less reliance on dense supervision.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: latent goal inference → separate agent vs. scene state → goal‑conditioned rollout → rendered egocentric frames
Before/after example: input short egocentric clip vs. multi‑second simulated continuation conditioned on an inferred goal
Timeline visualization showing predicted camera trajectory, hand contact events, and object state changes over rollout
Icon set: camera/head, hands, object interactions, and a goal/flag to symbolize intent conditioning
